o.text:
From Proto-Turkic *sat- (“to sell”).
Cognate with Turkish satmak, Old Turkic [script needed] (sat-, “sell”), Kazakh сату (satuw, “to sell”), Uzbek sotmoq (“to sell”), Chuvash сот (sot), etc.
From Proto-Common Turkic *kārt- (“falcon, hawk”). Cognate with Turkish kartal.

From *aqsırmaq, from *aɣ-sı-r-, from *aŋ-sı-r-, from Proto-Common Turkic *aŋ.
Cognate with Turkish aksırmak, dialectal Turkish angsırmak, anksırmak, ansırmak, ağsırmak, Tuvan азырар (azırar), Western Yugur [script needed] (asïr-).
Alternatively, onomatopoeic.

From Old Anatolian Turkish [Term?] (“to trace”). Cognate with Turkish izlemek. Ultimately a derivation of Proto-Turkic *īŕ, *ï̄ŕ (“trace, furrow”), whence also Old Turkic [script needed] (iz, “footprint, trace”). By surface analysis, iz (“trace”) + -lə.
From Arabic عَرَفَة (ʕarafa). See Turkish arife.
